notes: Capability manifest seed: one declarative record per operation across both operation tables.
registry=operations is internal/operations (model-backed/analysed, 32 ops); registry=ops is internal/ops (deterministic, in-process, 37 ops).
Phase 1 scope: identity, registry, family, mechanism, I/O ports, requirement class, ordered backend preference, and consent weight.

cli (verb + flag list) is declared per AI operation and consumed by cmd/gen-capability; params_schema, technique binding, and label/presentation codegen land in later phases (docs/internal/CAPABILITY-MANIFEST.md).
consent_weight is the SSOT consumed by internal/safety; it never gates availability.
Deterministic ops run in-process: backends is empty and mechanism is always compute.
Conformance tests enforce vocabulary coverage, backend existence in the model seed, requirement/mechanism coherence, and I/O agreement.
params_schema (JSON Schema subset, validated by internal/paramschema) declares operation-specific knobs without a proto change; op_params carries them on the wire.
presentation (icon name + i18n label/desc keys) is consumed by the generated UI catalog; labels stay in i18n, not in the manifest.
Deterministic records omit mechanism/requires/consent_weight/backends: the registry implies all four, and the loader makes them explicit before validation.
withinFrame expresses the relational box rule (positive area inside 0..1) once, so object_removal/scene_geometry/segment need no hand validator.

engine (ai|analysis|compute|unwired) declares the runtime; it replaces the table-name discriminator so consumers stop keeping a second membership list. presentation.panel is the workspace surface, deliberately separate from family.
Deterministic stylistic treatments are family=edit: enhance is reserved for operations that raise fidelity (and every such operation is model-backed).
A compute manifest omits io when it is the engine default (one image in, one image out); four operations declare ports explicitly.
probe is declared like every other analysis operation (engine=analysis, mechanism=compute): it was the last operation served without a manifest.
A deterministic operation declares its workspace form under presentation.fields; the TS spec is generated from that declaration and validated against the OpParams descriptor.

manifests.summary: Generate an image from a text prompt
Transform an input image guided by a prompt
Edit an image from a natural-language instruction (identity-preserving)
Regenerate a masked region from a prompt
Expand an image beyond its borders, generating the new region from a prompt
Remove a masked object and fill the gap
Remove the background to transparency
Replace the background behind a masked subject from a prompt
Put the face from a reference image onto a target image (SFW only; local models, with a consent affirmation for non-local routes)

prompt.description: Wording for a general image-editing route (a cloud editor or FLUX.2 klein); the dedicated swappers ignore it. Default: replace the face of the first image with the face of the second.

seed.description: RNG seed for a general image-editing route (0 = random); the dedicated swappers are deterministic.

face_strength.description: How much of the source person's face the swap puts on the target: 1 is the full swap, 0 keeps the target's own face. Mixes the two identities, so the result is a face between the two people.

extent.description: How much of the person to carry over, as a named set of stages (see the extent declaration).

match.description: Stages to add to the extent, each independent: skin tone, hair style, hair colour, or the whole head.

skin_target.description: Which way the skin stage matches tone: toward the source person's skin (default) or toward the target's own visible body skin (hands and arms), so the face matches the body it sits on.

stages.prompt: Change only the hairstyle of the person in the first image so their hair has the cut, length, parting and texture of the hair of the person in the second image. Keep the face, expression, skin, clothes, pose and background of the first image exactly as they are.
Replace the head of the person in the first image (face, hair, ears and neck) with the head of the person in the second image. Keep the body, clothes, pose and background of the first image.

manifests.summary: Replace or restyle clothing, hair, or makeup on a masked region from a prompt
Recolour a masked region of an image to match the colour of a reference (skin tone, hair colour), keeping its own shading and texture

strength.description: How much of the transferred colour is blended in (default 1).

luminance.description: Share of the reference's lightness offset applied: 0 keeps the region's own brightness, 1 moves it to the reference's (default 0.5).

flatten.description: How far the region's colour variation may shrink toward the reference's (default 0.4).

feather_px.description: Edge softening in pixels so the change fades into its surroundings (default 4).

manifests.summary: Find the poses on a pose chart (a sheet of figures in a grid or any other arrangement) and return each pose's cell

grid.description: Pin the layout as ROWSxCOLS (for example 3x3) instead of finding the figures from the page.

gap.description: How far apart two drawings must be to be separate cells, as a share of the page's longer side (default 0.02).

padding.description: Margin added around each drawing, as a share of its size (default 0.03).

manifests.summary: Read the pose of the people in an image as body and hand keypoints (photos and line-art figures)

box.description: Read this one person only: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in pixels. Default: find the people (a drawing with no detectable person is read as one figure).

max_people.description: The most people to read when finding them (default 4).

prepare.description: How the image is made readable first: auto fills in a line drawing (the estimator reads photographs, and finds about half the joints of a bare outline) and leaves a photo alone; none reads the image as given; line_art always fills it in.

manifests.summary: Put a character, written or shown in a reference picture, in the pose of a photo, a line-art figure or one cell of a pose chart

pose_cell.description: The pose chart cell to use, numbered in reading order as pose_chart_split numbers them. Default: the whole image is the pose.

pose_grid.description: Pin the chart layout the cell number refers to, as ROWSxCOLS (default: find each figure from the page).

pose_prepare.description: How the pose source is made readable first (see pose_extract); auto fills in a line drawing and leaves a photo alone.

pose_strength.description: How strictly the picture follows the pose.

character_strength.description: How strongly the reference picture steers the character; higher keeps more of it, and starts copying its pose.

preset.prompt: full body photo of {prompt}, plain light grey studio background, soft studio lighting, sharp focus, photorealistic
preset.negative: deformed, extra limbs, extra fingers, bad anatomy, blurry, text, watermark, cropped, cut off

manifests.summary: Lay a second image into the first through a mask, with a grown, feathered seam (the changed hair of an edited photo onto the original)

grow_px.description: How far to widen the mask before blending, in pixels, so the seam falls outside what changed (default 6).
